ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J34/J34nB300.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Chaozong (朝宗禪師語錄): Chaozong Tongren calls the proposed location a clod of stubborn earth and asks what connection it has.

Senses.Explanation: There is none (沒) of the dealings, involvement, connection, or bearing named by the compound (交涉): 'there is no connection' or 'it has no bearing.' The records deploy this one literal sense in two ways. First, as a plain statement of no connection. Shitou says that speech and action have no connection (言語動用沒交涉), and his disciple replies that non-speech and non-action also have no connection (非言語動用亦沒交涉). Another line says, 'before the King of Awe-Voice, no connection' (威音已前沒交涉). Second, as a dismissive verdict on a wrong answer. Blue Cliff Record comments repeatedly use 'well, no connection!' (且喜沒交涉 / 且得沒交涉), meaning that the offered account misses the recorded matter. The verdict can itself be challenged: when a monk says 'well, no connection' (且得沒交涉), Yuanwu asks, 'Where is there no connection?' (什麼處沒交涉). Intensified forms include 'utterly no connection' (全沒交涉 / 總沒交涉, 115 combined hits (全沒交涉 22 and 總沒交涉 93)), often in the line that something has utterly no bearing on one's own share (於自己分上全沒交涉). The rhetorical question 'what connection is there?' (有甚麼交涉 / 有什麼交涉, 141 occurrences of 有甚麼交涉 and 128 of 有什麼交涉 in the corpus) states the same absence by question. The headword is repeatedly attested representing 264 works.

Senses.Explanation: Nothing to get hold of is the closing verdict in a recurrent formula of being bare and exposed; masters quote it, challenge anyone who merely repeats it, and still demand a further word beyond it. Dahui Zonggao makes the bare, exposed, nothing-to-grasp condition a prerequisite before looking at Yunmen's dried-shit-stick answer. Another Dahui address couples it with ordinary walking, sitting, eating, and warming oneself, but immediately says even this does not yet deserve the name patch-robed monk. Chushi Fanqi joins Nanquan's livelihood to Zhaozhou's breaking up the household and calls the resulting nothing-to-grasp condition delightful. Yinyuan Longqi places it after roundness, exposure, and emptiness; Yi'an Shanzan says even this condition must answer when an ancient buddha meets a pillar; Zhikongyun quotes the whole older formula and then sets his own barrier.

Senses.Explanation: Having no handle to grasp renders the image literally as having no nose-handle: no projecting part by which a thing can be seized or led. The corpus is well attested. Chan records apply it to sayings, circumstances, people, and what a listener confronts. Dahui pairs it with ‘no flavor’ and says there is nothing to grasp when considering the dry shit-stick or a raised saying. Another record reverses the phrase into a direction for inquiry: investigate until there is no handle, and precisely there is a good place to investigate. Wuzhun plays the positive and negative forms against each other. The repeated bend is the point at which a word or encounter supplies no graspable lead.

Senses.Note: 6 exact full-case witnesses from 6 independent works support this corpus-bounded sense.

Senses.Explanation: Lacking flavor or being tasteless is predicated of sayings, inquiry, food imagery, and an interlocutor’s appraisal. A verse on Nanquan’s ‘ordinary mind is the Way’ calls it cold, bland, and entirely without flavor, yet says each raising is new. Dahui repeatedly places a person where bringing up the matter feels tasteless, like a lump of hot iron or biting an iron spike, and calls that a good place that must not be abandoned. Later records join nowhere to set a hand, lack of flavor, and the road of mind cut off; one calls the school’s tea and rice iron-nail rice and wood-chip soup and then calls the tasteless place good. The phrase can also remain adverse: a questioner calls Dahui’s answer flavorless and Dahui hisses. The records bend the sensory predicate by applying it to words and sustained inquiry in both appraising directions.

Senses.Explanation: The stringless lute is an impossible instrument that can nevertheless be requested, played, or heard in an encounter; its lack of strings is the point of the test. 8 passages across 8 distinct works show the wording in use; the witnesses include Meixi Fudu, Folang Xingxing, Guannan Daowu, Yulin Tongxiu, and later witnesses.

Senses.Note: Productive forms confirm the ordinary track-and-trace grammar: "absolutely no trace to seek" (the full “absolutely no trace to seek” form; 11 occurrences), and the bare trace predicate; the latter has 381 frozen-corpus hits and is not a ten-occurrence subformula. The direct question "what is the place where the hidden body leaves no trace?" (如何是藏身處沒蹤跡) occurs in five texts. The paired answers preserved here—"the moon sets, and the pool has no reflection" (月落潭無影) and "clouds arise, and the mountain has clothing" (雲生山有衣)—show how later records continue to ask each half separately. Across these forms the headword remains a trace predicate.

Senses.Explanation: The Boatman’s dominant paired injunction says: where you hide the body, leave no trace; where no trace remains, do not hide the body. Literally, to have no tracks or traces: "leave no trace" or "be without a trace." The phrase is broadly attested. The shorter place-form "where no trace remains" (沒蹤跡處) is well attested. Its dominant Chan use is Decheng the Boatman's injunction to Jiashan: "where you hide the body, leave no trace; where no trace remains, do not hide the body" (藏身處沒蹤跡，沒蹤跡處莫藏身), which is also turned into paired interview questions. Elsewhere the phrase stands as a short predicate: a person "going away" is described as "silent and still, leaving no trace" (寂寥寥沒蹤跡), in contrast with a person "coming back" who is "bright and distinct, with news" (明歷歷有消息). Another verse pairs "no trace" (沒蹤跡) with "news cut off" (斷消息). These are the direct contrasts recorded in the corpus.

Senses.Note: The evidence limits this entry to the immeasurable great person of Chan address.

Occurrences.Kwic: 龍門石和尚木主入祖堂，諸法姪請上堂，擊拂子云：「此是虎穴龍淵，鸞巢鳳窟，一切人無敢措足。除非沒量大人，方能移乾轉坤，喚東作西。所以道：『向這裏去則易，向那邊來則難。』二俱不立，中間不住，一柄石傘，蓋覆無邊，一脈耶溪，潤澤群有。」旋拂云：「收圓結果，仍到此間。」噓一聲云：「雨餘泉響隔華谿，谿上芹芽長玉犀，大家相聚喫莖虀，隔林猶有鷓鴣啼，謾看白雪踏烏雞。」

Occurrences.Kwic: 請同門信和尚，立僧上堂。「調烈馬為神駒，全藉孫陽鞭策；斲凡材成美器，必希郢匠斧斤。此是世間獻奇暴異之小技也。當知衲僧家有沒量大人，胸襟含裹太虛，眼光爍破天下。有時緊閉門墻，霜風凜冽，佛來魔來莫能窺測；有時豁開戶牖，和氣藹然，若愚若智盡屬獎提。以此劻勷祖道，祖道愈光；以此化育人天，人天欽仰。所以欲振祖父赫奕宗猷，須得兄弟同心努力。秖如山門騎卻佛殿、廚庫闖入僧堂，是何節目？」顧左右，曰：「勸君莫只空搔首，細問知音當自知。」

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂，僧問：如何是西來意？師曰：築著額頭磕著鼻。曰：意旨如何？師曰：驢駞馬載。曰：向上還有事也無？師曰：朝到西天，暮歸唐土。曰：謝師答話。師曰：大乘砑郎當。僧退，師乃曰：僧問西來意，築著額頭磕著鼻，意旨又如何？驢駞并馬載，朝到西天暮歸唐，大乘恰似砑郎當。何故？沒量大人被語脉裏轉却。遂拊掌大笑，下座。

Occurrences.Kwic: 師云看見了不柰何者多既看見如何却不柰何秖為不識所以不柰何若看見識得便柰何得也然發心叅禪便要會得誰不願樂秖為無箇入處又強會不得一切處不契合一切處緣差用力取不得良久云你十二時中行住坐臥折旋俯仰種種事業一切處有超佛越祖底事秖是你纔要解會時已無也󷹋箇是無也你擬湊泊已背了也所以道看見秖是不柰何莫是不擬心不起解會時得麼展轉更是不得也會尚不得豈況不會若是靈利底人纔聞山僧󵘸向你便能大開眼見得豈不是沒量大人向道是法非思量分別之所能解又道智不到處若不如此爭稱佛法而今兄弟家秖是呈箇解會呈箇見處作道理何曾解恁麼來何曾得到恁麼田地來若是有道種性底人肯恁麼去覰須是深深地體究密密地看詳忽然柰何得便無疑情也你等不明秖為十二時中被雜念奪將去也蓋為你要學事業見物便愛見文字便愛尋逐時便緣特去也道業何由得辦凡學事業人各有時三十已上便不可學也學亦難成學得又何用若己事辦去學亦得在蓋已點化了也若己事辦又豈肯學也若二十上下猶可學若是靈利念生死之人亦不肯學也又凡是叅禪須是心地平直心口相應心言直故如是始終地位無委曲相莫道我會也我柰何得也若柰何得那裏更去問人也你纔󵘸會禪也人覷你脚手看你󵘸話所為底事因甚却道者箇如何那箇如何既是會禪又却是爭無明也秖如道默耀韜光是如何藏名晦跡又如何不異人心是道又如何各自省緣莫󵘸是非且如行住坐臥進退俯仰一切處皆是超佛越祖山前水牯牛有佛法你纔尋究則已無也何不恁麼識取久立。
